SOLUTIONS.title: Add a 'good value' indicator to comparable deals
SOLUTIONS.summary: Add a 'good value' indicator next to comparable deals so travellers can tell at a glance which options are worth a closer look.
SOLUTIONS.ratingWhy: High-ish value because search abandonment is a real, measured problem, and effort is moderate since it builds on existing comparison data rather than new infrastructure.

SOLUTIONS.title: Surface key fare differences in the comparison list
SOLUTIONS.summary: Surface baggage allowance and key fare differences directly in the comparison list, instead of requiring a click into each option.
SOLUTIONS.ratingWhy: Moderate value, this is a floated idea rather than something tested with real travellers yet.
flags: No research document beyond the journey map itself for this one.

SOLUTIONS.title: Clear payment status after a failed attempt
SOLUTIONS.summary: Show a clear, unambiguous payment status screen immediately after any failed payment attempt, so travellers know whether they were charged.
SOLUTIONS.ratingWhy: High member value since an ambiguous failed payment is genuinely distressing, business value high since it likely drives support contacts down.

INSIGHTS.text: There are too many similar-looking deals, I can't tell what's actually a good price
I liked seeing 'price is trending down' on a route I was watching
My payment failed and I don't know if I was charged or not
Paying with my saved card in one tap was great
It kept prompting me to create an account after I'd already paid as a guest
Changing my dates sent me to a page that felt disconnected from my actual booking

OPPS.text: HMW make it clearer which deals are genuinely good value, so travellers can compare confidently at a glance?
HMW surface baggage allowance and fare differences directly in the comparison list?
HMW make failed-payment status unambiguous, so travellers know immediately whether they were charged?

GAPS.gapTitle: No research explains why people leave without comparing
GAPS.mapSays: We know the number, but nothing in our research explains why travellers leave the search results page without comparing more than one option.
GAPS.discoveryNote: Discovery opportunity: a short exit survey on the search results page would tell us whether this is a trust problem, a content problem, or people comparison-shopping elsewhere.
